description: ticket-init.sh does not validate the ticket type argument before writing to the tracker, allowing arbitrary directory traversal.
ticket-init.sh creates ticket files with world-writable permissions (0666) making ticket state tamper-able by any local user.
ticket-init.sh fails to sanitize newlines in the title argument, enabling multi-line injection into the event-sourced log.
ticket-exists.sh performs an unquoted glob expansion on the ticket ID that silently matches unrelated files when the ID contains shell glob characters.
ticket-exists.sh returns exit code 0 for both 'exists' and 'error reading directory', masking filesystem permission errors from callers.
test-batched.sh passes unsanitized user-supplied --test-dir value directly to find without quoting, allowing command injection via specially crafted directory names.
test-batched.sh accumulates all test runner PIDs in a single array without a maximum cap, enabling runaway memory usage on large test suites.
test-detect-stack.sh uses `ls` output parsing instead of glob or find, breaking on filenames with spaces and producing false negatives in stack detection.
test-detect-stack.sh does not reset the detection state between test cases, causing the second test to inherit stale findings from the first.
test-batched.sh captures stderr from child processes into a shared temp file without locking, leading to interleaved error messages when tests run in parallel.
